steps.body: Here's the twist. The rectangle club has ONE rule: four square corners. Does a square have four square corners? Yes! So **every square is also a rectangle** — a rectangle that happens to have equal sides too. The square is a rectangle wearing extra rules.
Does the square pass the rectangle test?

widget.prompt: Walk a square up to the rectangle club's door.

panels.title: The rectangle's one rule
panels.body: To enter the rectangle club, a shape needs four straight sides and four square corners. That's the whole entry test.

panels.title: Check the square against it
panels.body: A square has four straight sides ✓ and four square corners ✓. It passes every part of the rectangle test.

panels.title: So the square gets in
panels.body: The square meets the rectangle's rule, so it IS a rectangle — just a special one that ALSO has four equal sides. Extra rules don't lock it out; they make it stricter.

widget.continueFeedback: Keep going — see whether the square clears the door.
widget.successFeedback: A square passes the rectangle test, so every square is a rectangle. The equal-sides rule is a bonus, not a barrier.

predict.prompt: Every square is a rectangle. Is every RECTANGLE also a square?

options.label: No — the arrow runs one way
Yes — the club goes both ways
Neither is really the other

predict.reveal: The square's club has a stricter door — all sides equal — and most rectangles can't pass it. Membership flows up the hierarchy, never automatically back down.

explanationVariants: A square has four square corners, which is the rectangle's rule — so yes, every square is a rectangle.
The square meets all the rectangle's requirements and simply adds one more (equal sides), so it stays inside the rectangle club.

options.label: Yes — a square has four square corners, so it passes the rectangle rule
options.feedback: It meets every rectangle requirement and adds equal sides on top. A square is a special rectangle.

options.label: No — squares and rectangles are totally separate
options.feedback: They overlap: the square passes the rectangle's four-square-corners test, so it lives INSIDE the rectangle club.

options.label: No — a rectangle can't have equal sides
options.feedback: The rectangle rule says nothing AGAINST equal sides — it only requires square corners. Equal sides are allowed, making a square.

options.label: Only sometimes, depending on size
options.feedback: Size never matters here. EVERY square, at any size, meets the rectangle rule — so all squares are rectangles.

steps.body: But watch the arrow's direction — it only points ONE way. Every square is a rectangle, but **not every rectangle is a square.** A 6-by-3 rectangle has square corners yet unequal sides, so it fails the square's extra rule. The strict club fits inside the loose one, never the reverse.

explanationVariants: A long rectangle has square corners but unequal sides, so it fails the square's equal-sides rule — not every rectangle is a square.
The inclusion runs one way: squares fit inside rectangles, but a 6-by-3 rectangle can't meet the stricter square rule.

options.label: No — a rectangle with unequal sides fails the square's equal-sides rule
options.feedback: Squares are the STRICTER club. A 6-by-3 rectangle has square corners but not equal sides, so it isn't a square.

options.label: Yes — squares and rectangles are the same thing
options.feedback: They overlap but aren't equal. Every square is a rectangle, but a long rectangle can't pass the square's equal-sides rule.

options.label: Yes — all four-sided shapes are squares
options.feedback: Four sides only makes a quadrilateral. The square needs square corners AND equal sides — most rectangles miss the second.

options.label: Only if the rectangle is red
options.feedback: Color is a costume, remember. What blocks a long rectangle from being a square is its UNEQUAL sides.

widget.prompt: Order these clubs from the LOOSEST (most members) to the STRICTEST (fewest), as nested boxes.

misorderFeedback.feedback: The square is STRICTER than the rectangle — it adds the equal-sides rule, so it has fewer members. Rectangle comes first.
Quadrilateral is the loosest club of all (just 4 sides). The rectangle adds a rule, so it nests inside quadrilateral.

widget.missFeedback: More rules = stricter = fewer members = smaller inner box. Fewest rules goes first.
widget.successFeedback: Quadrilateral ⊃ Rectangle ⊃ Square — each inner club adds a rule and fits inside the last.

explanationVariants: The true direction is strict-fits-in-loose: a square (strict) is always a rectangle (loose), never the reverse.
Adding rules shrinks the club, so the square sits inside the rectangle, which sits inside quadrilateral.

options.label: Every square is a rectangle, but not every rectangle is a square
options.feedback: The strict club (square) fits inside the loose one (rectangle) — one-way inclusion, stated exactly right.

options.label: Every rectangle is a square, but not every square is a rectangle
options.feedback: That's the arrow backwards. The STRICT shape (square) is always the loose one (rectangle), not the other way around.

options.feedback: They do overlap — every square lives inside the rectangle club by meeting its four-square-corners rule.

options.feedback: A 6-by-3 rectangle has unequal sides, failing the square rule — so this can't be true for every rectangle.

hints: A square meets the rectangle rule (square corners), so it earns the rectangle label too.
It also has 4 sides, so it's a quadrilateral.
Which label does it NOT earn — is a square always a trapezoid?
explanationVariants: A square is a rectangle (square corners) and a quadrilateral (4 sides) — both guaranteed. The trapezoid is a different branch, defined by having just one pair of parallel sides; a square doesn't fit that 'just one pair' rule, so it doesn't automatically wear the trapezoid label.
Square earns rectangle and quadrilateral by meeting their rules; the trapezoid branch (just one parallel pair) is a different rule a square doesn't match, so that's the odd one out.

widget.prompt: A shape is a square. Which label does it NOT automatically earn?

options.label: Trapezoid
options.feedback: A square meets the rectangle and quadrilateral rules, but the trapezoid is a separate branch (just one parallel pair) — a rule a square doesn't match, so not automatic.

options.label: Rectangle
options.feedback: A square DOES earn 'rectangle' — it has four square corners, the rectangle's rule. Look for the label it misses.

options.label: Quadrilateral
options.feedback: A square has four sides, so it IS a quadrilateral. The label it doesn't automatically earn is elsewhere.

options.label: Four-sided shape
options.feedback: A square has exactly four sides — that label fits for sure. Find the one that isn't guaranteed.

takeaways: A square passes the rectangle's rule, so every square is a rectangle.
Not every rectangle is a square — inclusion runs strict-into-loose, one way only.
More rules = stricter club = smaller box nested inside the looser one.

concept.body: Quick rewind. Think **a square is a rectangle that got stricter** — it kept the square corners and ADDED equal sides. Because it still has square corners, it never left the rectangle club. But a plain rectangle didn't add the equal-sides rule, so it can't claim the square title.
